raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Implement `SupportsEagle3` for `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` and `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM` (which also serves `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`), so Granite MoE models can serve as targets for aux-hidden-state speculative decoding (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) and for `extract_hidden_states`. Follow-up to #60855, which did the same for dense `GraniteForCausalLM`.

## Claims

- Granite MoE targets (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`, `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM`, `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`) can now attach aux-hidden-state drafters and run `extract_hidden_states`. Previously, engine init rejected them because `supports_eagle3` was absent.
- The captured hidden states match HF `output_hidden_states` at the requested layers.
- No behavior change when no aux layers are requested: the models return `hidden_states` exactly as before.

## Validation

Hidden states extracted with `method="extract_hidden_states"` and `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`, compared with HF transformers `output_hidden_states` on the same token ids (3 prompts, up to ~450 tokens, bf16, GB200):

`ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct` (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`, 24 layers)

| Layer | Tokens | Mean cosine | Min cosine | Rel. error | Max abs diff |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 533 | 0.999943 | 0.999575 | 1.06e-02 | 3.12e-02 |
| 2 | 533 | 0.999924 | 0.997680 | 1.24e-02 | 3.12e-02 |
| 12 | 533 | 0.999406 | 0.989650 | 4.57e-03 | 1.60e+01 |
| 21 | 533 | 0.999151 | 0.978144 | 5.49e-03 | 1.60e+01 |
| 23 | 533 | 0.999116 | 0.981229 | 6.43e-03 | 1.60e+01 |

`ibm-granite/granite-swash-3b-a600m` (`GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`, served by `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM`; 28 layers, shared experts, sliding-window layers)

| Layer | Tokens | Mean cosine | Min cosine | Rel. error | Max abs diff |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 483 | 0.999945 | 0.997765 | 1.07e-02 | 9.38e-02 |
| 2 | 483 | 0.999892 | 0.997899 | 1.48e-02 | 9.38e-02 |
| 14 | 483 | 0.998695 | 0.978420 | 5.11e-02 | 6.25e-01 |
| 25 | 483 | 0.999317 | 0.971637 | 3.70e-02 | 2.25e+00 |
| 27 | 483 | 0.999377 | 0.975209 | 3.57e-02 | 4.00e+00 |

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k 'GraniteMoeForCausalLM or GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM or GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM'  # 3 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py  # 9 passed
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/granitemoe.py vllm/model_executor/models/granitemoeshared.py  # passed; mypy skipped locally (Python 3.10 host), left to CI
```

## Details

Same pattern as #60855. The inner models inherit `EagleModelMixin` and record hidden states with `_maybe_add_hidden_state` in the layer loop. The outer `*ForCausalLM` classes declare `SupportsEagle3`. `granitemoeshared.py` has its own model class and layer loop (it does not reuse `GraniteMoeModel.forward`), so both files need the change. Aux hidden states over pipeline parallelism stay unsupported for these models (`supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` is left `False`), as in #60855.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

LGTM. To validate DFlash inference, I created a dummy [config.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33387865/config.json) and ran a workload. Result: 128 successful reqs, 0 failures.

server:
```shell
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve \
  ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8123 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"triton"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"./dummy-dflash","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_load_config":{"load_format":"dummy"}}'
```

bench:
```shell
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8123 \
  --model ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 \
  --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 128 \
  --max-concurrency 8 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
  --seed 0 --save-result --result-filename benchmark.json
```
